provenance: I authored the Unique formalization and its additional evaluation checks, but did not author Shared or the correspondence implementation. For this cross-layer review I read all required authored units, exact Lean selections and the review-policy snapshot; I also inspected the named definitions and statement assumptions in any additionally listed source context. I compared the Shared design independently, found and requested correction of a stored-mode/path-mode wording mismatch, then reread the changed shared.steps snapshot and verified other required inputs unchanged before deciding. Listing a containing source context records the inspected definitions, not an audit of every proof tactic in that file.
rationale: unit:shared.syntax now introduces C, f, n, x, p, e and t before their grammar; unit:given.programs supplies the named class-table and sequence conventions, with given.classes/given.syntax giving their prerequisite domains. The selected Shared syntax has exactly variable/field places, give/giveShare places and recursive new with List Value, one destination/value statement, and class-table/body programs. It has no surface place-to-value coercion, share-of-arbitrary-expression form, assignment or borrowed reference form. Inspected Eval in context:lean/Shared/Step.lean gives the evaluation claims their intended meaning: giveShare first performs Give then changes its returned mode; EvalArgs threads left-to-right storage; Step.letValue requires a fresh destination. Names are represented as strings and class tables as lists; class/field uniqueness is a separate well-formedness condition, consistent with the chapter's later state definition rather than a claim that the raw syntax type enforces it.
limitations: This comparison checks prose/notation and formal statement correspondence; it does not independently certify Lean proof checking or audit proof tactics.
Lean uses raw lists for tables; finite-map reading and single-slot identity rely on the explicitly separate key-distinctness/well-formedness conditions.
